## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Titles with accented or non-Latin characters produce damaged or empty slugs because `slugify` matches only ASCII letters and digits, unlike the "non-alphanumeric" rule the description gives. The description also lacks the `## Testing` section that project policy requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify` function that lowercases a title, collapses runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into single hyphens and trims hyphens from the ends. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters or transliterate them in slugify — The title `"Café Menu"` becomes `"caf-menu"`, `"Über uns"` becomes `"ber-uns"`, and `"日本語"` becomes `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says the function replaces "non-alphanumeric characters", but `str.isalnum` treats `é` and `日` as alphanumeric. — Pages with non-English titles get truncated URLs, and titles made only of non-Latin characters all share an empty slug. — Fix: Either normalize with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks before matching, or use `[^\w]+|_` so Unicode letters are kept, then add a non-ASCII case to `test_slugify` in `tests/test_slug.py`.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the description — The description has only a one-sentence summary and no `## Testing` section, which breaks AGENTS.md:4: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Maintainers cannot tell from the description whether or how the new tests were run.
